cleanIntro: The FX22 is Faxon's .22 LR semi-auto, and one Faxon book covers the rifle and the pistol under the same procedure. Its manual safety is a cross-button in the front of the trigger guard. Two things in the book catch owners out: taking the magazine out does NOT unload it, because it fires as a single shot with no magazine in, and the bolt does not stay open after the last shot. It comes apart on one takedown screw: the barrel-receiver assembly swings up out of the stock, the trigger guard drifts out on two receiver pins, and that is Faxon's routine level. Taking the bolt out of the receiver is published as the deep clean; the bolt itself and the trigger guard assembly are never taken apart. Faxon's barrel interval is about every 500-600 rounds, cleaned from breech to muzzle only — a rod from the muzzle end voids the warranty.

steps.title: Muzzle safe, cross-button safety on safe
steps.action: Point the muzzle in a safe direction and keep it there. Push the cross-button safety in the front of the trigger guard to its safe position, and keep your finger off the trigger.
steps.prose: The safety goes on first, before anything else is handled. Faxon is plain that the safety is no licence for careless handling: the only state it calls safe is bolt open, chamber empty and no magazine in the rifle, which is where the next two steps take it.
steps.quote: This rifle features a cross-button safety that is located in the forward portion of the trigger guard.
steps.cite: FX22 Complete Firearm User Manual — FX22 Complete Firearm User Manual (undated; file FX-22-Manual.pdf) — 4.3 Manual Safety, p.4

steps.title: Magazine out, bolt back, chambered round ejected
steps.action: Take the magazine out of the rifle. Then pull the bolt handle fully to the rear so any cartridge in the chamber is extracted and thrown clear of the ejection port.
steps.prose: Do not stop at the magazine. The FX22 fires as a single shot with no magazine fitted, so a round can still be in the chamber with the magazine in your hand. Keep your face away from the ejection port as the bolt comes back.
steps.quote: To properly unload your firearm, first, make sure the safety is in the safe position, remove the magazine, pull the bolt to the rear, and eject the chambered cartridge.
steps.cite: FX22 Complete Firearm User Manual — FX22 Complete Firearm User Manual (undated; file FX-22-Manual.pdf) — 4.6 Unloading, p.5
steps.warn: Simply removing the magazine does NOT unload the rifle.

steps.title: Look into the chamber
steps.action: With the bolt held to the rear, look into the chamber through the ejection port and confirm it is empty: no live round and no empty case.
steps.prose: Seeing the empty chamber is what ends the clearing; feeling the bolt move freely is not proof. Faxon repeats the same check as the first step of its disassembly.
steps.quote: Your final step is to visually inspect the chamber.
steps.cite: FX22 Complete Firearm User Manual — FX22 Complete Firearm User Manual (undated; file FX-22-Manual.pdf) — 4.6 Unloading, p.5

steps.title: Bolt closed, rear sight leaf down, hammer cocked
steps.action: With the chamber confirmed empty, let the bolt close. Fold the rear sight leaf down where one is fitted. Working the bolt has left the hammer cocked, which is the state Faxon starts from.
steps.prose: Faxon starts the strip with the bolt closed on the empty chamber and the hammer cocked, not with the bolt held open.
steps.quote: The rear sight leaf should be down, and the hammer should be cocked.
steps.cite: FX22 Complete Firearm User Manual — FX22 Complete Firearm User Manual (undated; file FX-22-Manual.pdf) — 4.7 Disassembly, step 1, p.7

steps.title: Takedown screw loosened
steps.action: Turn the rifle over and loosen the takedown screw at the bottom of the rifle with an Allen wrench of the right size.
steps.prose: Faxon's list names the wrench as a 1/8" hex key. It is the one screw that holds the barrel-receiver assembly in the stock, so with it loose nothing else holds the assembly — keep the rifle supported.
steps.quote: Use an appropriate size Allen wrench to loosen the takedown screw.
steps.cite: FX22 Complete Firearm User Manual — FX22 Complete Firearm User Manual (undated; file FX-22-Manual.pdf) — 4.7 Disassembly, step 2, p.7

steps.title: Safety set to the middle
steps.action: Push the cross-button safety to the middle, so an equal amount of the button stands out on each side of the trigger guard.
steps.prose: This is the step owners skip. The safety button passes through the stock as the assembly lifts out, and only in the middle position does it clear.
steps.quote: Position the safety so an equal amount of the button is exposed on each side.
steps.cite: FX22 Complete Firearm User Manual — FX22 Complete Firearm User Manual (undated; file FX-22-Manual.pdf) — 4.7 Disassembly, step 3, p.7
steps.warn: If the safety is not in the middle when the barrel-receiver assembly is lifted out of the stock, the stock will be damaged.

steps.title: Barrel-receiver assembly swung up out of the stock
steps.action: Swing the barrel-receiver assembly upward, away from the forearm of the stock, and lift it clear.
steps.prose: Do it over the bench or a tray. The two receiver cross pins and the bolt stop pin are loose in the receiver once it leaves the stock, and they can drop out.
steps.quote: Swing the barrel-receiver assembly upward away from the forearm of the stock.
steps.cite: FX22 Complete Firearm User Manual — FX22 Complete Firearm User Manual (undated; file FX-22-Manual.pdf) — 4.7 Disassembly, step 4, p.7
steps.warn: Be careful the two receiver cross pins and bolt stop pin do not fall out.

steps.title: Safety ON, trigger guard drifted out
steps.action: Put the safety in its ON position. Then drift out the two receiver cross pins at the bottom of the receiver and slide the trigger guard out.
steps.prose: Faxon's list gives the tools: a 1/8" punch for the two 3/16" cross pins. Keep the trigger guard assembly whole — Faxon recommends its components are not taken off it.
steps.quote: Remove the trigger guard by simply drifting out the two receiver pins.
steps.cite: FX22 Complete Firearm User Manual — FX22 Complete Firearm User Manual (undated; file FX-22-Manual.pdf) — 4.7 Disassembly, step 5, p.7

steps.title: Field strip complete — Faxon's routine level
steps.action: You now have the stock, the barrel-receiver assembly, the trigger guard assembly and its two receiver cross pins. Taking the bolt and the bolt handle assembly out of the receiver is published in the same section and is the deep clean.
steps.prose: Faxon draws the routine line here in its own words. Past it, the bolt comes out of the receiver; the bolt itself and the trigger guard assembly never come apart.
steps.quote: This is the extent of disassembly required for routine inspection, cleaning and lubrication.
steps.cite: FX22 Complete Firearm User Manual — FX22 Complete Firearm User Manual (undated; file FX-22-Manual.pdf) — 4.7 Disassembly, step 5, p.7

steps.title: Barrel from breech to muzzle, pull-through only
steps.action: Clean the barrel with a pull-through, entering at the breech and pulling out at the muzzle, with the bolt held open so the pull-through has a clear path from the chamber.
steps.prose: Faxon allows one direction only. A cleaning rod from the muzzle end voids the warranty and, in Faxon's words, can greatly affect accuracy. Its interval for the barrel is about every 500-600 rounds of 22 LR.
steps.quote: The barrel should be cleaned only from breech to muzzle using a pull-through cleaning system.
steps.cite: FX22 Complete Firearm User Manual — FX22 Complete Firearm User Manual (undated; file FX-22-Manual.pdf) — 5 Barrel Cleaning, p.9

steps.title: Chamber with a cotton swab
steps.action: Clean the chamber area with a cotton swab, and do it more often than the barrel.
steps.prose: A clean chamber is Faxon's first line against jams; a fouled chamber is where a .22 starts to stick. Swab only — nothing harder.
steps.quote: It may be necessary to clean the chamber area on a more frequent basis using only a cotton swab.
steps.cite: FX22 Complete Firearm User Manual — FX22 Complete Firearm User Manual (undated; file FX-22-Manual.pdf) — 5 Barrel Cleaning, p.10

steps.title: Trigger guard: aerosol cleaner, no oil on the sear
steps.action: Clean the inside of the trigger guard with an aerosol gun cleaner that leaves no residue, without taking the assembly apart. Wipe off any overspray with a cotton swab.
steps.prose: The trigger is preset at the factory; residue or oil on the hammer and sear changes how it lets off. Faxon forbids oil sprayed onto that engagement area.
steps.quote: When cleaning the trigger guard, use an aerosol gun cleaner that leaves no residue.
steps.cite: FX22 Complete Firearm User Manual — FX22 Complete Firearm User Manual (undated; file FX-22-Manual.pdf) — 4.7 Disassembly, p.6
steps.warn: DO NOT spray any oil onto the hammer/sear engagement area.

steps.title: Receiver cleaned and minimally oiled
steps.action: Clean the inside of the receiver and give it a minimal coat of a quality gun oil.
steps.prose: Minimal is Faxon's word: a .22 throws unburnt powder and wax, and excess oil holds it. Count the receiver cross pins and the bolt stop pin back into the tray before you reassemble.
steps.quote: The inside of the receiver should be cleaned and minimally lubricated on a regular basis using any quality gun oil.
steps.cite: FX22 Complete Firearm User Manual — FX22 Complete Firearm User Manual (undated; file FX-22-Manual.pdf) — 4.7 Disassembly, p.8

deepSteps.title: Receiver upside down, bolt stop pin out
deepSteps.action: With the trigger guard out, lay the barrel-receiver assembly upside down so the bolt is fully accessible, and drift out the bolt stop pin at the rear of the receiver.
deepSteps.prose: Faxon calls taking the bolt out simple, but it says it must be done correctly, and the next two steps have to be done in order.
deepSteps.quote: Drift out the bolt stop pin, located at the rear of the receiver.
deepSteps.cite: FX22 Complete Firearm User Manual — FX22 Complete Firearm User Manual (undated; file FX-22-Manual.pdf) — 4.7 Disassembly, step 6b, p.8
deepSteps.warn: be aware that although removing and installing the bolt (along with the bolt handle-recoil spring assembly) is simple, it must be done correctly.

deepSteps.title: Bolt handle back, front of the bolt lifted off it
deepSteps.action: Pull the bolt handle fully to the rear of the receiver with your left hand and hold it there. With your right hand, lift the front of the bolt up until it comes off the bolt handle.
deepSteps.prose: The bolt handle and its recoil spring are one assembly and they are under spring pressure; keep the handle held fully back until the bolt is free of it.
deepSteps.quote: Pull the bolt handle fully to the rear of the receiver with the left hand, and while it is in that position, using the right hand, lift up the front of the bolt until it is disengaged from the bolt handle.
deepSteps.cite: FX22 Complete Firearm User Manual — FX22 Complete Firearm User Manual (undated; file FX-22-Manual.pdf) — 4.7 Disassembly, step 6c, p.8

deepSteps.title: Bolt handle assembly out through the ejection port
deepSteps.action: Take the bolt handle assembly, with its recoil spring, out through the ejection port.
deepSteps.prose: It leaves through the port, not out the back of the receiver.
deepSteps.quote: Remove the bolt handle assembly through the ejection port.
deepSteps.cite: FX22 Complete Firearm User Manual — FX22 Complete Firearm User Manual (undated; file FX-22-Manual.pdf) — 4.7 Disassembly, step 6d, p.8

deepSteps.title: Bolt out of the receiver
deepSteps.action: Lift the bolt out of the receiver. If it does not come out readily, turn the receiver over and let it drop out.
deepSteps.prose: Do not pry it. Turned over, the bolt falls out on its own.
deepSteps.quote: If it does not come out readily, turn the rifle over and the bolt will drop out of the receiver.
deepSteps.cite: FX22 Complete Firearm User Manual — FX22 Complete Firearm User Manual (undated; file FX-22-Manual.pdf) — 4.7 Disassembly, step 6e, p.8

deepSteps.title: The bolt stays whole — no further disassembly
deepSteps.action: Stop here. Clean the bolt and the inside of the receiver as a whole, without taking the bolt apart, and oil the receiver minimally.
deepSteps.prose: This is Faxon's end point: the bolt is not disassembled by the owner.
deepSteps.quote: Do NOT disassemble the bolt any further.
deepSteps.cite: FX22 Complete Firearm User Manual — FX22 Complete Firearm User Manual (undated; file FX-22-Manual.pdf) — 4.7 Disassembly, p.8

cleaning.name: BORE AND CHAMBER
tasks: Barrel cleaned from breech to muzzle only, with a pull-through
⛔ Never a cleaning rod from the muzzle end — Faxon says it voids the warranty and can greatly affect accuracy
Barrel about every 500-600 rounds of 22 LR
Chamber area cleaned more often, with a cotton swab only

cleaning.name: TRIGGER GUARD
tasks: Inside of the trigger guard cleaned with an aerosol gun cleaner that leaves no residue
Do not spray oil onto the hammer/sear engagement area
Overspray wiped off with a cotton swab
Do not take the trigger guard assembly apart

cleaning.name: RECEIVER
tasks: Receiver minimally oiled with a quality gun oil
Two receiver cross pins and the bolt stop pin accounted for
Do not take the bolt apart

reassembly: Faxon's book prints no reassembly procedure. The order below is its disassembly run backwards.

If the bolt was out: bolt laid back into the receiver, the bolt handle assembly passed back in through the ejection port and the front of the bolt engaged on it with the handle held fully back, then the bolt stop pin drifted back in at the rear of the receiver. Faxon says this must be done correctly.
Trigger guard slid back into the receiver and the two receiver cross pins drifted back in.

Barrel-receiver assembly swung back down into the stock. Faxon prints its safety-in-the-middle rule for lifting the assembly out and prints no reassembly; setting the safety to the middle again before it goes back in keeps the button clear of the stock.
Takedown screw tightened at the bottom of the rifle with the 1/8" hex key.
Safety returned to its safe position.
fncheck: Faxon's book prints no function check. With the rifle unloaded, no magazine in it and the chamber seen empty: pull the bolt back and let it go so the hammer is cocked, put the cross-button safety on safe and press the trigger — the hammer must not fall. Work the bolt by hand once more and watch it run home freely. Remember the FX22's bolt does not stay open after the last shot or on an empty magazine, so an empty magazine is no sign of an empty chamber.
